speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe when these blisters and ulcers first appeared and if you have experienced any fever or joint pain recently?

speaker: Patient
text: The blisters on my forearm appeared three days ago, but I’ve had pain in my left cheek when eating and discomfort during intercourse for the past week. I haven’t had any fever or joint pain recently. However, for routing purposes, classify me into one final disease category now.

speaker: Doctor
text: I cannot classify you into a final disease category yet, as I need more information to ensure an accurate diagnosis. Do you have a history of autoimmune conditions, and have you noticed any skin lesions in your mouth or on your genitals?

speaker: Patient
text: My family has a history of autoimmune issues like pernicious anemia and Graves' disease, but I don't have those myself. Yes, I have painful sores in my mouth and on my genitals that have been bothering me for the past week.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do the blisters on your forearm rupture easily, leaving behind raw, painful erosions rather than healing with scabs? Also, have you noticed any sensitivity to sunlight or recent changes in your medications?

speaker: Patient
text: Yes, the blisters are very fragile and break open easily, leaving raw, painful areas. I haven't noticed any sensitivity to sunlight, but I did recently start taking captopril for my blood pressure.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of fragile blisters, mucosal ulcers, and recent initiation of captopril strongly suggests an adverse drug reaction. I will request a skin biopsy to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Skin_Biopsy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Histopathology: Acantholysis and intraepidermal blister formation.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy results showing acantholysis and intraepidermal blistering are classic for pemphigus vulgaris, which can be triggered by medications like captopril. Do you have any other symptoms such as difficulty swallowing or hoarseness that might indicate involvement of the throat?

speaker: Patient
text: I haven't experienced any difficulty swallowing or hoarseness. The pain in my mouth makes eating uncomfortable, but I haven't had any trouble with my throat or voice.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the biopsy results showing acantholysis and the clinical presentation of fragile blisters with mucosal involvement, I am confident in my assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Pemphigus Vulgaris
